messages.author: eafdb2ba12ece80e
messages.subject: bin2d and size
parts:
Hi,

I am a beginner of ggplot2, but I do have two separate questions that
might be related.

1. I have been using bin2d for a 2D- histogram. However, the scale of
the colors that represents the data density is different for each data
set - I wish to create a homogeneous scale for all my plots for
different data set, how could I achieve that?

2. When I create a scatter plot, i set size = a variable. This
variable actually represents the standard deviation measure, so I
would like the size of each data point to be proportional to the
numerical value of that variable, and I would like to have control
over their relationship. How could I achieve this?

Thank you a lot in advance! It would be good if you could point me to
some directions, tutorials, etc, that could possibly resolve my
issues :)

Best,
Fantasista

messages.subject: Re: bin2d and size
parts:
Hi Hadley,

Thanks so much for your reply!

I do not think scale_fill_continuous works for my purpose. Let me
describe the problem again.

I have a set of 60 similar data sets to make into 60 2D histogram
plots, and on each of them, the color (intensity) scales differently
depends on the spread of the data in each plot. Suppose at the point
in the plot with x-axis = 10 and y-axis = 10, in one data set a color
blue might represent 20 data point on this point in the plot, in
another data set a color blue might represent 25 data points. I wish
to have control over that, i.e., a homogeneous way of saying, 20 data
points -> blue, 25-> darker blue, 30-> even darker blue, etc. I think
scale_fill_cont lets me set the color for the minimum data intensity,
as well as the maximum, but the scaling is computed automatically,
which differs from one graph to another.

For the second problem, I meant that, if i use
geom_point(aes(size=stdev)), the size of each circular data
representation will depend on the value of the stdev variable.
However, the size is not proportional to the stdev variable - now if I
have stdev = 1 and stdev = 99, the size of the latter might be twice
in diameter of the former - but I wish it to be 99 times larger of the
former. How do I get control over that? I believe this is a similar
problem as the previous one.

Thank you!

Fantasista

messages.subject: Re: bin2d and size
parts:
> I have a set of 60 similar data sets to  make into 60 2D histogram
> plots, and on each of them, the color (intensity) scales differently
> depends on the spread of the data in each plot. Suppose at the point
> in the plot with x-axis = 10 and y-axis = 10, in one data set a color

> another data set a color blue might represent 25 data points. I wish
> to have control over that, i.e., a homogeneous way of saying, 20 data
> points -> blue, 25-> darker blue, 30-> even darker blue, etc. I think
> scale_fill_cont lets me set the color for the minimum data intensity,
> as well as the maximum, but the scaling is computed automatically,
> which differs from one graph to another.

Have a look at the limits argument, that stops the limits from being
automatically calculated and allows you to set them to what you want.

> For the second problem, I meant that, if i use
> geom_point(aes(size=stdev)), the size of each circular data
> representation will depend on the value of the stdev variable.
> However, the size is not proportional to the stdev variable - now if I
> have stdev = 1 and stdev = 99, the size of the latter might be twice
> in diameter of the former - but I wish it to be 99 times larger of the
> former. How do I get control over that? I believe this is a similar
> problem as the previous one.
scale_size(to = c(0, 10), limits = c(0, 100))

Hadley

Hi.
I'm transitioning to R from Matlab and SAS and just trying some basic things. However, I seem to be having problems understanding the data structures and how ggplot2 understands them. Here is my problem.

> summary(A)
V1 V2 V3 V4
Min. :-74.76 Min. :-52.93 Min. : 1.0 Min. :2005
1st Qu.:-70.53 1st Qu.:-42.34 1st Qu.:155.5 1st Qu.:2006
Median :-66.84 Median : 32.95 Median :224.0 Median :2007

3rd Qu.:-65.68 3rd Qu.: 76.57 3rd Qu.:290.0 3rd Qu.:2008
Max. :-61.47 Max. :115.53 Max. :365.0 Max. :2009
> ggplot(A$V2,A$V1,aes_string(x="Boo",y="hoo"))
Error in ggplot.data.frame(fortify(data), mapping, ...) :
Mapping should be created with aes or aes_string

I've created A using the following:

setwd("/Volumes/Geospatial001/IcebergIII/data/level1")
library("ggplot2")
#

png(filename = "Rplot.png", res = 300)

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 and R newbie with simple, simple problem
parts:
Try

ggplot(data=A,aes(x=V1,y=V2)) + geom_point()

or

qplot(V1,V2,data=A)

With ggplot() it's common to provide the dataframe as an unnamed first argument (rather than using data=). Eitherway, that argument is the dataframe, the aes is a mapping from the columns of the data frame to graphical parameters. It's easier if you give your column names semantically meaningful names. And remember that qplot() and ggplot() are two quite different interfaces to the ggplot2 library.

It would help if you used dput() to provide sample data, as described in the email footer:
> Please provide a reproducible example: http://gist.github.com/270442
--J
